title: McPAL: Scaling Unstructured Sparse Inference with Multi-Chiplet HBM-PIM Architecture for LLMs
problem: Monolithic PIM architectures cannot scale to very large LLMs (70B+) due to single-die memory footprint limits; LLM inference is memory-bound, and PIM can provide high memory bandwidth but scaling via larger dies hits power/yield constraints.
motivation: LLMs are growing rapidly (Llama-70B+); monolithic PIM chips cannot accommodate the memory footprint, requiring chiplet-based multi-PIM scaling.
method: Multi-chiplet HBM-PIM architecture (McPAL) that decomposes arbitrary unstructured sparse weight matrices into multiple irregular sparse vectors, then routes non-skipped computations via in-memory butterfly network to standard PIM arrays. Vertically scales via 3D-HBM hierarchy (minimizing long-distance data travel) and horizontally via 2.5D IO chiplet (reducing die-to-die traffic and balancing sparse workload).
key_novelty: Hierarchical multi-chiplet PIM scaling with in-memory butterfly network for arbitrary unstructured sparsity, avoiding monolithic bottlenecks.
contributions: Multi-chiplet PIM architecture for LLM inference scaling
In-memory butterfly network for unstructured sparse routing
Vertical 3D-HBM scaling with minimized long-distance data travel
Horizontal 2.5D IO chiplet for balanced sparse workload distribution
1.57–3.12× speedup over A100 GPU; 10.43–35.66× energy efficiency
limitations: Evaluation limited to Llama models (7B–70B); applicability to dense or structured-sparse models not discussed; comparison with recent sparse inference accelerators (BitNet, etc.); multi-chiplet communication latency overhead not quantified.
primary_theme: hierarchical multi-chiplet PIM with butterfly network for scalable sparse LLM inference
